meta.source: Prepared local public snapshot (fresh-root candidate). Every projection below is illustrative: it transcribes documented, test-pinned semantics of the snapshot into a static view. No new experimental results were generated.

reliabilityContract.note: These are contract classifications of a machine-readable claim catalog, not a quality score. 7/15 is not a rating.

scenarios.failureMode: Conflating a logical task with its executions. If a task_id were reused as the identity of an attempt, expressing "ran it again" would require overwriting history — the first attempt's failure record would be destroyed.
sequence: one logical task_id
attempt 1 → new run_id, appended
attempt 2 → new run_id, appended
attempt 3 → new run_id, appended
attempt ordinals are derived from durable run_started events, never from an in-memory counter

table.caption: Illustrative projection of retry semantics: one task_id, three attempts, three distinct run_id values
rows: failed — stored as a fact, never erased
success — committed as a third record

scenarios.preserved: All three records remain in the append-only event history. The eventual success does not overwrite the failures; per-attempt status and task-level outcome stay separable.

evidence.label: Task / Run data model (logical vs attempt identity)
attempt ordinal derived from durable starts

scenarios.nonClaim: This does not demonstrate exactly-once execution, deduplication, or any real-provider behavior. The runtime deliberately rejects duplicate attempt identities instead of deduplicating them.

scenarios.failureMode: A crash between dispatching external work and committing its outcome. If recovery treats a missing success record as permission to repeat the action, an already-executed (possibly billed) invocation is silently duplicated.
sequence: run_started persisted
provider_invocation_started persisted immediately before the call
process interrupted before outcome/terminal could be committed
fold projects: ambiguous_external_execution
resume returns AMBIGUOUS — no provider invocation

table.caption: Durable execution-state projection (documented contract; fold and resume decisions)

scenarios.preserved: Uncertainty itself. A durable invocation without a committed successful terminal is never automatically re-invoked unless durable evidence proves a retryable failure. Ambiguity is preserved across restarts rather than resolved by guessing.

evidence.label: RC-13 ambiguity preservation / RC-15 safe retry

scenarios.nonClaim: This demonstrates preservation and fail-closed recovery, not resolution. No reconciliation mechanism, no external-repair API, and no proof that the ambiguous invocation did not execute externally exists (RC-14: NOT_SUPPORTED).

scenarios.failureMode: Re-judging a stored output against a silently changed specification. If the mutable current task definition were the scoring reference, a later spec edit would rewrite the meaning of every historical judgment.
sequence: run executes with expected = "Paris"; the run persists expected_snapshot = "Paris"
output returned: " paris " (edge whitespace, different case)
current task fixture is later edited to expected = "London" (drift)
v1 (exact) judges the run: FAIL — against the snapshot, never "London"
v2 (normalized) judges the same run: PASS — same snapshot reference

table.caption: Illustrative projection: one stored run, two evaluator versions, one immutable reference

scenarios.preserved: Judgment identity is the pair (run_id, evaluator_version). Each version's verdict is a separate durable record; execution metrics are invariant across evaluator versions; a run without a captured snapshot is not eligible for new evaluation at all (no current-task fallback).
scenarios.nonClaim: Version binding establishes which semantics produced a judgment. It does not establish that any evaluator version measures output quality validly, nor anything about model quality.

scenarios.failureMode: Collapsing different questions into one rate. Coverage, per-attempt reliability, recovery, and output quality have different denominators; merging them turns "nothing was evaluated" into a fake 0.0 and hides quarantined records inside an average.
sequence: four report signals, four explicit denominators
raw vs valid vs quarantined counts are all exposed, never hidden
an undefined ratio is emitted as null, not 0.0
structural contradictions abort the report entirely (no numbers at all)
referential violations and ambiguous duplicate judgments are quarantined and listed

table.caption: The four report signals (Signal Semantics v0) — each answers a different question

scenarios.preserved: Quarantined observations stay visible: an evaluation referencing a nonexistent or failed run, or an ambiguous duplicate (run_id, evaluator_version) group, is excluded from every denominator and listed in the report's integrity block. Failed evaluator runs appear as raw counts, never as silent zeros.
scenarios.nonClaim: No end-to-end task pass rate exists (deliberately deferred), and no metric here says anything about model quality or about the scientific validity of any evaluation.

supports: Logical task identity and execution-attempt identity are distinct, durable, and test-pinned.
Retries append new history; committed results are immutable across resume and replay.
Ambiguous external execution is preserved and blocks automatic re-invocation (fail closed).
Evaluations bind (run_id, evaluator_version) and judge only the execution-time snapshot.
Report denominators are explicit; undefined ratios are null; invalid records are quarantined, not averaged in.
A machine-readable reliability contract classifies every claim with named evidence tests.
nonClaims: No real LLM/provider integration — the agent is a deterministic mock plus injected faults.
Single process, single writer; no database, queue, or web service.
No exactly-once provider execution and no event-idempotent append (RC-10/RC-14: NOT_SUPPORTED).
Not production-grade infrastructure: append+flush is not fsync, transactional, or concurrent-writer safe.
Not a model-quality benchmark and not an evaluation-methodology validation.
Malformed returned output can be committed as execution success (no output schema validation).

nonGuarantees.name: Event replay idempotence
nonGuarantees.detail: Duplicate events fail loudly; they are not deduplicated. No idempotency key or exactly-once append.

nonGuarantees.name: Failure replay determinism
nonGuarantees.detail: Replay accepts successful snapshot-bearing runs only; failed runs are not replayable.

nonGuarantees.name: Exactly-once provider execution
nonGuarantees.detail: Uncertainty is preserved and automatic replay blocked, but external execution cannot be proven either way without reconciliation.

nonGuarantees.name: Cost / token budget safety
nonGuarantees.detail: No cost or token budget subsystem exists; the only budget is the request-attempt budget (RC-02).
